title: Treasure Bag
brief: A list lets you keep many things in one variable, all in order. Your Treasure Bag starts with two items, then you'll add a new one with .append(), count everything with len(), and show the whole bag. Fill in the three lines, then press Check Project!
steps: The bag already holds "sword" and "shield", and the program asks the user for a new treasure.
Add the new item to the end of the list using bag.append(new_item).
Print how many items are in the bag now using len(bag).
Print the whole bag with print(bag).
Run it, add a treasure, then press Check Project.
starterCode:
# 🎒 Treasure Bag, collect items in a list!

bag = ["sword", "shield"]

new_item = input("What treasure do you want to add? ")

# 1) Add new_item to the end of the bag using .append()
# bag.append(new_item)

# 2) Print how many items are in the bag now (use len):
# print("Items in bag:", len(bag))

# 3) Print the whole bag:
# print(bag)
inputHint: Type one treasure to add to the bag.
successMessage: Nice haul! 🎒 Your list grows with .append(), counts itself with len(), and keeps everything in order. That's exactly what lists are made for!
